cohort: 207 women who gave birth at a university hospital in Sweden between 2009-2016 (69 in the PCA group and 138 in the EDA group)
finding: Intravenous remifentanil patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) was associated with shorter active labor and a higher rate of spontaneous delivery compared to standard epidural analgesia (EDA) without worsening maternal or neonatal morbidity or women's satisfaction with delivery.
mod_finding: PCA was associated with a higher rate of spontaneous delivery compared to EDA.
